judged_text: The imported-from footer interpolates url into single-quoted HTML with only a `^https?://` regex guard, so a quote in the URL path escapes the href attribute (HTML5 tokenization starts a new attribute even without whitespace). An attacker who can place a link on the embedding host (e.g. a blog comment linking to /embed/best?embed_url=http://host/?s='onclick='...) supplies a referer that passes the embeddable_host check and an embed_url whose host passes TopicRetriever's host check while its query string carries the payload; the resulting raw_html post stores the injected event-handler attribute and executes on the Discourse origin when the topic is viewed.

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the code appends an "imported from" footer using `"#{url}"` and then stores it as `raw_html` (`PostCreator.new(... cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])`), and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. The only validation on `url` is `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or other HTML-breaking characters in the URL. Therefore a crafted URL containing a single quote can break out of the `href='...'` attribute and inject additional attributes/JS, leading to XSS on Discourse origin when the cooked/raw HTML is displayed.
